issuer.name: Third National (under licence from Visa) — international programme; programme operated by Ether.Fi Cash Ltd.

funding.supported_assets_note: 'Borrow Mode': purchases are funded by USDC borrowed through the Aave LendGateway (Optimism) against assets in the user's Vault (USDC/USDT/EURC/frxUSD, liquidUSD/liquidEUR, weETH/WETH, eBTC, ETHFI, OP, tokenised stocks…); a 'Direct Pay' mode spending from the Vault balance also exists but is not described in detail on the pages read. Settlement currency USD or EUR.

credit_terms.liquidation_risk: Borrowing interest accrues (rate not stated on the help page; 'check the app or the GitBook parameters page'). Product LTV is per collateral asset: 81% stablecoins (USDC, USDT, EURC, frxUSD), 80% liquidUSD/liquidReserve/liquidEUR, 55% weETH/WETH, 52% eBTC, 50% liquidETH/liquidBTC, 20% ETHFI/sETHFI/OP. Legacy Cash DebtManager: 50% of collateral liquidated first when the position exceeds its limit, remainder if still unhealthy; liquidation thresholds 95% stablecoins, 75% weETH/WETH, 70% liquid ETH/BTC, 50% OP/ETHFI, with 1–5% liquidation bonus to the liquidator. The agreement lists a 'Liquidation Fee (Reserved)' and a returned-payment fee.

variants.region_label: International (non-US) — 86 listed countries incl. most of the EEA, UK, CH

eligibility.nationality_restrictions_note: International cardholder agreement: 'strictly prohibited for use by U.S. persons'; users must not be blocked or sanctioned by the US government; 18 years or older.
eligibility.usage_note: Countries named by the help centre as able to receive a physical card (no ISO codes; mapping is ours) plus Belgium and Ireland (eligible, virtual card only — no physical delivery). 'If a jurisdiction is not listed, you cannot apply' → unlisted = ineligible. Malaysia and South Africa appear in the availability list AND in the prohibited-jurisdictions list: modelled as excluded (least favourable). Puerto Rico is listed but is a US territory covered by the US-persons prohibition — left out. Colombia is listed as eligible while the restricted-regions page lists Colombia among countries where 'spending is unsupported'. Spending unsupported in KP, IR, RU, SY, CU, VE, MM, UA, CO. The United States (31 listed states, issuer not read) is a separate programme under a different agreement — not modelled here. Lists carry no date and are 'subject to change'.

kyc.stages_note: KYC during account setup; 'Approval is required before a Cash card can be issued'. Government-issued passport, national ID or driving licence; 'advanced liveness check' selfie; proof of address (<3 months) 'in some cases'; a card-issuer questionnaire and extra documents may be requested by jurisdiction. Most reviews within 48 h. Crypto deposits need no verification; bank transfers need a separate bank-transfer verification. Provider not named.

fees.conditions: Physical card $50 for Core (no free physical card; max 1). Virtual card: 1 free then $10 each (max 5) — 'some regions charge Core members $10 for their first virtual card' (regions not named). Modelled on the physical card.
Core membership is free; no card annual fee stated.

Applies to transactions in a currency other than USD or EUR, rate set at settlement. Help centre: Core 0.5% added FX fee. Cardholder agreement (fee info 'as of April 15th, 2025'): base 1% foreign transaction fee plus 'up to an additional 50bps' for Core. Governing value (David, 2026-11-02, policy rule 5): the dated cardholder agreement — 1.5% modelled. The help-centre figure is shown as a contradiction.
'Free, up to 10 withdrawals per month' for Core; the fee beyond the allowance is in a separate article not read. Limits: $5,000 per withdrawal, 5 attempts and $25,000 per rolling 24 h (all levels).

Excluded transaction types/merchants listed in a separate article (not read); refunds reverse cashback.

evidence.title: What are the benefits of a personal Cash credit card? (help centre)
evidence.excerpt: Visa Signature. Cashback 3% on first $2,000 (Core) / $10,000 (Luxe) / $50,000 (Pinnacle), 4% on $50,000 (VIP); EUR caps $800/$3,000/$16,000. Category cashback Luxe 10% to $10/mo, Pinnacle 20% to $20, VIP 30% to $30. Virtual card $10 after free ones; physical $50 (Core) / $100 (Luxe, Pinnacle). ATM 'Free, up to 10 withdrawals per month' (Core, Luxe), 'Free, unlimited' (Pinnacle, VIP). No date.

evidence.excerpt: Core: free starting level. Luxe: 5K points to activate + 5K/month, or $15K Liquid, or 30K ETHFI staked, or $199/yr. Pinnacle: 25K points, or $100K Liquid, or 150K ETHFI, or $999/yr. VIP: $500K Liquid or 500K ETHFI staked, no annual purchase. Points: Cash 1,000 per $1k spent; reset monthly. No date ('Updated over 2 weeks ago').

evidence.title: How does cashback work? (help centre)
evidence.excerpt: 'Eligible cashback is earned in ETHFI'; converted at clearing price, 7-day lock. Monthly bands: Core 3% first $2,000 / 1% to $3,000 / 0.5% above; Luxe 3% to $10,000 / 1% to $20,000 / 0.5%; Pinnacle 3% to $50,000 / 1% to $80,000 / 0.5%; VIP 4% to $50,000. EUR bands lower ($800/$3,000/$16,000; 0.1% top band). Shared USD+EUR counter, resets monthly. Exclusions in a separate article.

evidence.title: What's the foreign exchange (FX) rate used on Cash transactions? (help centre)

evidence.contradiction_note: The cardholder agreement states a base 1% foreign transaction fee plus up to 50 bps (Core) / 25 bps (Luxe); this article shows only 0.5% / 0.25% / none. The dated agreement is modelled (1.5% / 1.25% / 1%).

editorial.summary: Visa card funded by a crypto-collateralised USDC credit line (or direct payment from an on-chain Vault), available in 86 listed countries outside the US including most of the EEA, the UK and Switzerland. Free Core level pays 3% in ETHFI on the first $2,000 a month; paid Luxe ($199/yr) and Pinnacle ($999/yr) levels raise the 3% band to $10,000 and $50,000. Foreign-currency fee and several other fees are contradictory or unknown across official pages.
good_for: Holders of ETH/weETH, stablecoins or ether.fi Liquid vaults who want to spend without selling (borrow mode)
Residents of the listed EEA countries, the UK and Switzerland who accept a USD/EUR-settled card and ETHFI-denominated cashback
High spenders willing to pay for Luxe or Pinnacle to lift the 3% band
not_for: US persons (prohibited under the international agreement; a separate US programme exists and is not documented here)
Residents of Estonia, Finland, the Netherlands, Turkey, India, Indonesia, Malaysia or South Africa (prohibited)
Anyone who wants cashback in fiat or a stablecoin: rewards are paid in ETHFI after a 7-day lock
Borrowers who cannot absorb liquidation of their collateral if prices fall
watch_outs: Foreign-transaction fee is contradictory: the help centre says 0.5% (Core) / 0.25% (Luxe) / none (Pinnacle, VIP) while the dated cardholder agreement states a base 1% plus up to 50/25 bps — the agreement's higher figures are modelled.
The Fee Schedule referenced by the agreement, the ATM fee after 10 free withdrawals, the top-up fee and the borrowing APR were not read — recorded as unknown, never as free.
Malaysia and South Africa are listed both as available and as prohibited; Colombia is eligible but spending there is 'unsupported'.
Cashback steps down to 1% then 0.5% (0.1% for EUR) above the monthly bands; EUR bands are far lower ($800 for Core).
Borrow mode carries liquidation risk; legacy terms liquidate 50% of collateral first.
